title: Handle Missing Values and Errors
summary: A program can meet a problem, such as a missing number. You can check for the problem and give a clear reply instead of using a bad value.
introduction: A program can meet a problem, such as a missing number. You can check for the problem and give a clear reply instead of using a bad value. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Catch an error and show a clear message
Check whether an optional has a value
Choose a fallback when a value is missing

blocks.text: throw reports an error. try starts work that may report one. catch handles a matching error. Here, dividing by zero is stopped before it happens.

blocks.text: Show that a value may be missing
optional<int> holds a whole number or nothing. Check it first. The star reads the number only after we know it is there.

blocks.title: errors-exceptions.cpp

blocks.text: value_or supplies a value when the optional is empty. Here we show 0 when no score was entered.

blocks.title: errors-exceptions.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: Never read an empty optional with *. Check it or use value_or. C++23 also has expected for a value or an error; the examples here use C++20.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Give score a value of 9 in the last example. Check the new output.
